question: What is the primary mission of the CSSD in a healthcare facility?

options.A: Treating patients with severe blood infections
options.B: Providing sterile supplies and controlling infection
options.D: Disposing of hazardous clinical waste safely

explanation: The core function of the department is to process and issue sterile medical devices to prevent hospital-acquired infections. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h1)

question: Why is standardization of protocols important within the CSSD?

options.A: It guarantees uniform safety and reliability of sterilized items
options.B: It reduces the need for protective clothing among staff
options.C: It speeds up instrument manufacturing processes in the hospital
options.D: It lowers the financial cost of purchasing new surgical tools

explanation: Uniform protocols ensure that every single instrument undergoes the exact same rigorous cleaning and sterilization standard. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h1)

question: What type of air pressure is required in the decontamination zone?
explanation: Negative pressure prevents contaminated air and aerosols from escaping into clean corridors and adjacent rooms. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h2)

question: A patient tray passes from the wash area to the packing room. What is the correct airflow direction?

options.A: From clean zones towards the decontamination zone
options.B: From clean packing into the dirty decontamination room
options.C: Airflow direction has no impact on infection control
options.D: From the sterile storage area out into the corridor

explanation: Air must flow from clean areas to dirty areas so airborne contaminants are pushed away from sterile supplies. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h2)

question: Why must instruments be cleaned before undergoing sterilization?

options.A: Clean instruments take up less space in the autoclave
options.B: Dry blood makes the instruments look unprofessional
options.C: Washing prevents the metal from melting during the cycle
options.D: Organic matter shields microorganisms from the sterilizing agent

explanation: Residual blood or protein acts as a barrier, preventing steam or chemicals from reaching and killing the microbes. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h3)

question: How do ultrasonic cleaners remove debris from narrow instrument hinges?

options.A: Through cavitation caused by collapsing microscopic bubbles
options.B: By using extreme heat to burn off stubborn grease
options.C: By dissolving the metal surrounding the hidden dirt
options.D: Through high-speed rotation of stainless steel brushes

explanation: Ultrasonic waves create tiny bubbles that implode violently, pulling dirt out of microscopic crevices and box locks. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h3)

question: What is placed inside instrument trays before wrapping to verify steam penetration?
explanation: Indicator strips react to parameters like heat and steam, confirming the sterilant reached the inside of the pack. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h4)

question: A nurse discovers a hemostatic forceps with a loose box lock during assembly. What is the appropriate action?

options.A: Apply machine oil and place it directly into the sterile tray
options.B: Package it anyway since the autoclave will fix the joint
options.C: Remove the instrument from the set for repair or replacement
options.D: Send the instrument straight to the patient care ward

explanation: Damaged instruments compromise patient safety and clinical efficiency, so they must be removed from circulation. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h4)

question: What is the most common and reliable method for sterilizing heat-stable surgical instruments?
explanation: Steam sterilization is fast, effective, economical, and leaves no toxic residue on standard metal instruments. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h5)

question: A nurse is loading an autoclave with wrapped instrument trays and heavy basins. How should items be arranged?

options.A: Items packed tightly against the chamber walls for fast heating
options.B: Stacked flat on top of each other to maximize chamber space
options.C: Basins placed directly on top of delicate paper-plastic pouches
options.D: Packs on edge and basins arranged to prevent trapping water

explanation: Placing items on edge allows steam to circulate freely and prevents condensation pools from forming on flat surfaces. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h5)

question: Which monitoring category uses spore-based test vials to confirm true microbial destruction?
explanation: Biological indicators contain actual living spores designed to test whether the sterilizer can kill highly resistant microorganisms. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h6)

question: What does a color change on an external chemical indicator tape confirm?

options.A: That the packaging material is completely free of tears
options.B: That all bacterial spores inside the instruments are dead
options.C: That the pack has been exposed to the sterilization process
options.D: That the autoclave reached the exact required pressure peak

explanation: Chemical indicators only show exposure to heat or steam; they do not prove that sterility was fully achieved inside the pack. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h6)

question: What does the FIFO inventory rule stand for in CSSD supply management?
explanation: FIFO ensures older sterile stock is distributed first to prevent items from sitting on shelves indefinitely. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h7)

question: When does a sterile instrument package lose its sterility in modern clinical practice?

options.A: Whenever a new shift of nursing staff comes on duty
options.B: After exactly seven days on a closed storage shelf
options.C: When the outer temperature drops below room level
options.D: When the packaging is torn, wet, or dropped

explanation: Sterility is event-related; packs remain sterile indefinitely unless an environmental event compromises the protective packaging barrier. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h7)

question: Which personal protective equipment is essential when washing instruments in the decontamination zone?

options.A: Sterile surgical gowns and powder-free gloves
options.B: Lead lined aprons and protective eyewear
options.C: Disposable paper caps and fabric lab coats
options.D: Waterproof aprons and heavy utility gloves

explanation: Decontamination workers need heavy gloves and waterproof aprons to protect against chemical detergents and contaminated fluid splashes. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h8)

question: Why are face shields required during manual instrument scrubbing in the wash area?

options.A: To keep steam from fogging up prescription eyeglasses
options.B: To comply with fire safety rules in high-temperature rooms
options.C: To prevent splashes and infectious aerosols from reaching the eyes and face
options.D: To prevent staff from breathing in dry dust particles from clean shelves

explanation: Manual scrubbing and brush use create fine mists and splashes that can transmit bloodborne pathogens through mucous membranes. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h8)
